portal_solution:
Before applying this update, make sure all previously-released errata
relevant to your system have been applied.

This update is available via the Red Hat Network. Details on how to
use the Red Hat Network to apply this update are available at
https://access.redhat.com/knowledge/articles/11258
portal_description:
Red Hat Identity Management is a centralized authentication, identity management
and authorization solution for both traditional and cloud-based enterprise
environments. It integrates components of the Red Hat Directory Server, MIT
Kerberos, Red Hat Certificate System, NTP, and DNS. It provides web browser and
command-line interfaces. Its administration tools allow an administrator to
quickly install, set up, and administer a group of domain controllers to meet
the authentication and identity management requirements of large-scale Linux and
UNIX deployments.

This update fixes the following bugs:

* Anonymous access to the Identity Management servers can be set to the
"rootdse" option, which means that anonymous clients can only access the rootDSE
LDAP entry. Previously, when all the configured Identity Management servers had
this option enabled, an attempt to enroll the Identity Management client using
the "ipa-client-install" command failed during the discovery phase. This update
provides a patch to fix this bug and "ipa-client-install" proceeds as expected
in the described scenario. (BZ#952741)

* Under certain circumstances, the Identity Management Certificate Authority
(CA) certificate stored in Directory Server was double encoded. This behavior
prevented some of the Identity Management clients from enrolling. With this
update, the CA certificates are encoded and stored in Directory Server properly.
(BZ#964128)

* Previously, the Identity Management server certificate subsystem did not set
the NSS database trust arguments properly after the renewal. Consequently, the
Identity Management server was unable to communicate with the certificate
system. The underlying source code has been modified and the trust arguments are
now set correctly after the renewal. (BZ#964130)

Users of ipa are advised to upgrade to these updated packages, which fix these
bugs.
